subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: During an empty plugin-scope reload, which agent harnesses, if any, should remain globally selectable: none, only approved always-on/native harnesses, or every previously registered harness?
rationale: The source-proven bug needs a fix, but the safe behavior is an ownership contract decision because restore-all semantics can override plugin disablement while clear-all semantics can drop active channel/cron turns.

options.title: Preserve Only Approved Harnesses
options.body: Filter preservation to the maintainer-approved always-on/native harness contract and keep disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses cleared, with loader and gateway coverage.

options.title: Preserve Every Previous Harness
options.body: Accept restore-all semantics for empty-scope reloads and document that previous plugin harnesses may survive until the next full reload or restart.

options.title: Defer To Broader Lifecycle Redesign
options.body: Pause the narrow PR and design a canonical immutable/request-scoped harness registry path that removes the global clear/restore window.

recommendation.title: Preserve Only Approved Harnesses
recommendation.body: Filter preservation to the maintainer-approved always-on/native harness contract and keep disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses cleared, with loader and gateway coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the clearest history owner for the harness registry and agent-runtime selection surface where the ownership contract must be decided.
